records.decision: Class BOOT/BUTTON/EN/I2C/LED=3.3 V with 0.00 mm added manufacturing margin.
records.justification: Dual-beacon-tag logic signals operate at 3.3 V with currents limited by pull-ups, LED resistors, or receiver inputs. These logic routes use the manufacturing minimum and no added current-derived margin.
records.no_alternatives_reason: These nets are standard 3.3 V logic signals whose manufacturing margin is determined by the fab minimum width; no alternative classification is applicable.

records.decision: Class CC1/CC2=5.0 V and USB_D-/USB_D+=3.3 V with 0.00 mm added manufacturing margin.
records.justification: Dual-beacon-tag USB-C CC signals and USB data lines operate at logic voltage. These nets are logic/current-minimum routes, so they use no added power-domain margin.
records.no_alternatives_reason: These are USB logic and configuration lines governed by interface geometry and the fab minimum line width; no alternative classification is applicable.

records.decision: Class VBUS=5.0 V/0.5 A, +3V3=3.3 V/0.5 A, GND=return with 0.00 mm added manufacturing margin.
records.justification: Dual-beacon-tag power nets carry the main supply current. The manufacturability is governed by the fab minimum line width; extra current-carrying width margin is reserved for the power domain rather than added to signal traces.
records.no_alternatives_reason: These power nets are classified by their voltage and current ratings as required by the design specification; no alternative net class is applicable.

records.decision: Control and sensor nets use the manufacturing minimum width basis.
records.justification: These are logic signal nets whose current is limited by pull-ups or LED resistors. Their trace width is governed by the fab minimum rather than a current-derived width basis.
records.no_alternatives_reason: The fab minimum width is sufficient for these logic signals; no alternative width basis is required.

records.decision: USB data and CC nets use the manufacturing minimum width basis.
records.justification: USB data lines and CC configuration signals are logic-level nets with minimal current. Their trace width is governed by the fab minimum.
records.no_alternatives_reason: The fab minimum width is sufficient for USB logic and configuration signals; no alternative width basis is required.

records.decision: Power nets use a width basis derived from the 0.5 A current limit.
records.justification: VBUS, +3V3, and GND carry the main supply current up to 500 mA. Their trace width basis is derived from the current limit rather than the fab minimum.
records.no_alternatives_reason: Power nets require a current-derived width basis; the fab minimum is insufficient for the rated current.

records.decision: VBUS is declared as a 5.0 V power rail sourced from the USB-C VBUS pin.
records.justification: The USB-C connector delivers 5 V via VBUS pins A4/A9/B4/B9, making VBUS the primary 5 V power rail for the design.
records.no_alternatives_reason: USB-C VBUS is the specified power input; no alternative power source is declared.

records.decision: +3V3 is declared as a 3.3 V power rail sourced from the AMS1117-3.3 regulator output.
records.justification: The AMS1117-3.3 LDO converts 5 V VBUS to 3.3 V, making +3V3 the regulated power rail for the MCU and peripherals.
records.no_alternatives_reason: The AMS1117-3.3 is the specified regulator; no alternative 3.3 V source is declared.
